text:
Cheng: Quick sync — yesterday's zone evacuation: we had a handful of requests stuck on the eu-west proxy during the handoff. Observed ~6s tails for warmup and some residency mismatches for customers with EU data-residency. Anyone captured logs?

Maria: I saw it in the ops dashboard. Proxy swap sequence completed but a couple tenants arrived at the new site without the X-Resident-Region header set, so they fell back to global routing. We surfaced billing and privacy flags in the logs.

Sam: I caught trace IDs 8f3a... and 9b2c... — looks like the proxy handoff flow didn't inject the header when the lease swap raced with the keepalive refresh.

Jen: FWIW the warmup step currently triggers a background prefetch that waits for model container ready; that adds ~4–7s if the cache is cold. We can pre-warm but need an operator hook.

Cheng: Two distinct problems then: header/ownership propagation (race) + cold-cache warmup tail. Both create user-visible latency or privacy mixing.

Sam: Proposal sketch: lightweight operator tool to assert residency and run a dry-run handoff. CLI prototype: 
```
# dry-run: validate all tenancy headers and priming
proxy-swap --tenant TENANT_ID --region eu-west --assert-residency --dry-run

# staged swap: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%
proxy-swap --tenant TENANT_ID --region eu-west --stage canary
```
This would call control-plane endpoints that coordinate RPCs to proxies/dataplane.

Maria: Legal/compliance note: we cannot 'relax' the strict-eu residency flag for tenants with PII. The operator tool must support per-tenant gating and an explicit human-ack for restricted tenants.

Jen: Implementation detail: add `POST /internal/prime-cache` endpoint to call model init + tokenizer load for a tenant/model combo so warmup is deterministic. Something like:
```
POST /internal/prime-cache
{ "tenant": "T-123", "model": "redwood-7b", "ttl": 300 }
```
Return: success + latency estimate.

Cheng: Question: who should perform the residency header write? Options: control-plane forces a lease bump and writes a cluster-wide header, or dataplane proxies coordinate a handshake to swap owner and then advertise header. Tradeoffs: CP bump is faster but increases blast radius and requires privileged ops; dataplane handshake is safer but slower and more complex.

Sam: I lean operator + CP-assisted assert for evacuation flows where we want minimal user latency. We'll need RBAC & audit and a kill-switch.

Maria: Agreed but enforce per-tenant policy checks before CP bump. Also add an emergency revert that flips a tenant back to previous region and invalidates any pre-warm caches.

ops-bot: action created: TI-4821 — "eu-west evacuation handoff - pre-assert residency" assigned to Sam. :white_check_mark:

Jen: Telemetry to add: `residency_mismatch.count`, `handoff_warmup.latency_p95`, `operator_stage.progress` (percent). Dashboards + alert thresholds (>0 mismatches).

Cheng: Next steps / owners: Sam -> RFC for operator pre-assert + staged swap API, include CLI examples and failure modes. Jen -> implement prime-cache endpoint + telemetry. Maria -> compliance gating + console UI for per-tenant overrides. I'll put together a brief follow-up doc and schedule a 30m sync next Tue.

Sam: Will draft RFC. Timeline: aim for draft by EOD Friday.

Maria: Add me to review — I’ll validate compliance flows.

Jen: I'll stub the prime-cache handler and add a test harness.

Cheng: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
